market_wrap.text: Nifty rose 1.85% to 25,819 and the Sensex about 1,500 points as markets reopened after Tuesday's holiday and won back Monday's fall. Record foreign buying in November, Brent crude slipping to about $90 and a rupee at an eight-month high lifted banks, IT and FMCG (Nifty FMCG +3.8%); metals were the only sector to fall.

reasons.reason: Silver kept sliding: MCX silver futures were down about 2% in the afternoon, near ₹1.42 lakh/kg, on fears of a US Fed rate hike, a 19-month-high dollar and fund selling ahead of US PCE inflation data. The ETF fell further than the futures and closed near its 52-week low.
MCX gold fell about 1.3% to around ₹1.20 lakh per 10 g on the same Fed-hike and strong-dollar worries; Gold BeES touched ₹99.90 intraday and is down more than 13% so far in November.
